q-111074.name: Question 1
q-111074.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $1+\sqrt{z}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1+\sqrt{z},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2{z}^{2}}{1-\sqrt{z}} & = \\ -\frac{2{z}^{2}}{1-\sqrt{z}}\cdot \frac{1+\sqrt{z}}{1+\sqrt{z}} & = \\ -\frac{2{z}^{2}(1+\sqrt{z})}{(1-\sqrt{z})(1+\sqrt{z})} & = \\ -\frac{2{z}^{2}(1+\sqrt{z})}{{1}^{2}-(\sqrt{z})^{2}} & = \\ -\frac{2{z}^{2}(1+\sqrt{z})}{1-z} & = \\ \frac{2{z}^{2}(1+\sqrt{z})}{z-1} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-34851.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $7-\sqrt{a}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $7-\sqrt{a},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{7+\sqrt{a}} & = \\ \frac{3}{7+\sqrt{a}}\cdot \frac{7-\sqrt{a}}{7-\sqrt{a}} & = \\ \frac{3(7-\sqrt{a})}{(7+\sqrt{a})(7-\sqrt{a})} & = \\ \frac{21-3\sqrt{a}}{{7}^{2}-(\sqrt{a})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{21-3\sqrt{a}}{49-a}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

Rationalize the denominator of 1w+w−3.

a
w−w−33
b
2(w−w−3)
c
3(w−w−3)
d
w−w−32
e
2(w−w−3)3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that the denominator's conjugate is w−w−3.

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate w−w−3, and simplify: 1w+w−3=1w+w−3⋅w−w−3w−w−3=w−w−3(w+w−3)(w−w−3)=w−w−3(w)2−(w−3)2=w−w−3w−(w−3)=w−w−33
